synoptic.summary: A weak, fast-moving trough crosses the Great Basin Sunday night. It brings a low chance of snow showers on the higher terrain Monday (2–3% at the launches, thunder 0%) and a 20–30% chance of clouds on the peaks Monday morning. Behind it the launch forecast turns the flow to 350°–20° all day Monday, so POM North works and POM South does not. A drier ridge crosses Tuesday into Wednesday with light flow, but the forecast keeps 140°–180° at the POM launches all of Tuesday — the usual afternoon switch to 320°–360° is not forecast until Wednesday around 14:00, ahead of another weak trough late Wednesday. The winds-aloft fetch failed this run, so rotor and mixing-down checks rely on the NWS mixed-layer (transport) wind only.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: As a fast-moving trough sweeps across the Great Basin tonight, modest moisture will gradually begin to infiltrate the lower levels, resulting in low precipitation chances on Monday primarily across higher terrain. Given weak dynamics and very limited moisture, rainfall/liquid equivalent will largely remain below 0.10" (90% chance).

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport read 1017.6 mb at 17:54 local Sunday, down from 1020.2 mb at 22:54 Saturday as the trough approaches. It bottomed at 1016.9 mb at 14:54 and has ticked up 0.7 mb since. A weak trough, not a strong gradient; the ridge rebuilds Tuesday.

observations.summary: Sunday evening readings, 16:15–17:50 local — about 13.5 h before the first slot, so they describe this evening, not Monday morning. Winds are light and variable: Salt Lake airport 320°/5 kt, Spanish Fork 350°/2 kt G4, Alpine 6°/5 kt G7, Lehi swinging 167°–214° at 1–3 kt, Provo calm. South Valley Regional's newest reading (16:35) has no wind; at 16:15 it had 350°/6 kt. Point of the Mountain and Draper returned no data.
